title: Meet the fan who caught Yankees’ George Lombard Jr.’s first home run
content:
NEW YORK — As the baseball screamed through the New York night and toward the left field seats at Yankee Stadium, Bruce Roberts grabbed the hat, purchased just 10 minutes earlier, off his head and thrust it in the air.

When he brought the Yankees cap back down, he couldn’t believe what he saw. Inside was the ball from George Lombard Jr.’s towering home run. It was the first career hit for New York’s top prospect, who was making his MLB debut on Tuesday night.

“Totally unexpected,” Roberts told The Athletic.

Lombard’s home run came in the fifth inning Tuesday, and gave the Yankees a 2-0 lead over the St. Louis Cardinals. Soon after it landed in Roberts’ cap, security approached the Utah resident, who attended the game with his wife, Marie, and his son, Cash. The family was at the game a gift for Cash’s 12th birthday.

Security asked if Roberts would be willing to give the ball to Lombard, whose parents, George and Judy, were also in attendance. Roberts agreed to a trade that consisted of three signed baseballs from Lombard and a chance to meet him after the game.

“No-brainer,” Roberts said. “They were really generous about it.”

Lombard, 21, was mobbed by his teammates after he rounded the bases and entered the dugout. His first career plate appearance came in the third inning, and he grounded out in a 1-2 count.

Roberts said that in the fifth, “everyone was going for” the home run ball.

“What a great experience,” he said, “to be able to go near the clubhouse and meet somebody that’s an up-and-comer. I never thought that was going to happen. It just makes it a really unique experience for me and my family.”

Roberts isn’t a Yankees fan, but he’s not a Yankees hater. He grew up in the Bay Area in California, rooting for the San Francisco Giants, and he is a coach on his son’s Little League team.

The family arrived in New York on Monday and is slated to head back home Friday. Cash, whose birthday prompted the trip, told his parents he wanted to see a slew of New York tourist attractions — the Statue of Liberty, the Sept. 11 memorial, a Broadway show and the Empire State Building.

And Cash, who is a pitcher, wanted to catch a Yankees game, which ended up being a smart idea. Roberts considered seats behind home plate or closer to the action. He bought the tickets just a few days ago.

“And I just thought this time,” he said, “let’s try the outfield. Somewhere in left or left-center field. Maybe one of the balls will come close and it will be exciting.”

Yep, good thought.

“Super exciting,” Roberts said.
